steps.tx: Renal cell carcinoma comprises distinct pathological and molecular entities originating from renal tubular epithelium. **Clear cell renal cell carcinoma** represents over seventy-five percent of cases and is driven by biallelic von Hippel-Lindau VHL gene inactivation on chromosome 3p. This defect impairs ubiquitin-mediated degradation, causing constitutive HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha transcription factor accumulation and overexpressing downstream angiogenic VEGF, PDGF, and GLUT-1.

steps.tx: Both scans show a large **enhancing renal mass** replacing much of the left kidney while the right kidney looks normal. The panel links **VHL loss** on chromosome 3p to **HIF accumulation** and then to **VEGF driven** vessel growth. Grasping this chain matters because the vascular appearance on contrast scans reflects the biology and points toward vessel blocking and HIF directed options.
steps.say: These contrast scans show a large enhancing mass in the left kidney, seen in coronal and axial views. The diagram traces the cause from VHL gene loss to HIF buildup and then to VEGF driven vessel growth. That biology explains the rich blood supply visible on imaging and why treatment targets vessel signals and HIF itself.

steps.tx: The diagram traces **VHL loss** on chromosome 3p to unchecked **HIF accumulation** in the nucleus switching on growth genes. Resulting **VEGF** plus PDGF flood builds the tangled hypervascular bed feeding clear cell kidney cancer. Seeing gene loss drive vessel growth explains sensitivity to vessel blocking drugs and later HIF directed pills.
steps.say: Loss of both copies of VHL stops the cell tagging HIF factors for disposal, so they pile up and join partners on DNA. That switch turns on signals that sprout a dense mesh of new blood vessels around the kidney tumour. The chain from gene loss to vessel excess is why clear cell cancer looks so bloody and why treatments aim at vessel signals and at HIF itself.

vis.alt: The diagram links VHL loss to HIF buildup and vessel rich kidney tumour growth.
vis.caption: Gene loss drives vessel rich kidney tumour growth. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Validated prognostic models guide systemic treatment selection and clinical trial stratification. The **IMDC model**, or Heng criteria, provides risk stratification into favourable, intermediate, and poor risk based on six clinical variables: Karnofsky performance status under eighty percent, diagnosis-to-treatment interval under one year, anaemia, hypercalcaemia, neutrophilia, and thrombocytosis. Patients with zero adverse factors achieve favourable survival exceeding forty-three months.

steps.tx: Combination systemic regimens have replaced single-agent VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in frontline advanced disease. In the landmark **KEYNOTE-426** phase 3 study, first-line combination of pembrolizumab plus axitinib significantly improves progression-free and overall survival compared to sunitinib monotherapy in advanced RCC. Objective response rate reached 60% with the combination versus 40% with sunitinib, demonstrating efficacy across all IMDC risk groups.

steps.tx: Dual immune checkpoint inhibition generates deep, durable responses. In **CheckMate 214**, nivolumab plus ipilimumab dual immunotherapy establishes superior overall survival and high complete response rates in IMDC intermediate- and poor-risk metastatic RCC. Complete response rates reached 12% in intermediate- and poor-risk cohorts, with long-term follow-up revealing sustained treatment-free survival plateaus in responding patients.

steps.tx: Alternative anti-PD-1 and TKI combinations offer exceptionally potent disease control. In **CheckMate 9ER**, cabozantinib plus nivolumab doubled progression-free survival over sunitinib. Similarly, the **CLEAR** trial showed lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab achieving a median PFS of 23.9 months and an objective response rate of 71%, proving superior overall survival and tumour debulking in bulky or symptomatic disease.

steps.tx: Downstream transcription factor targeting overcomes upstream receptor tyrosine kinase resistance. **Belzutifan** is a first-in-class oral small-molecule HIF-2alpha inhibitor approved for advanced clear cell RCC progressing after immune checkpoint and VEGFR-TKI therapy in LITESPARK-005. It binds allosterically to the PAS-B domain of HIF-2alpha, preventing heterodimerization with HIF-1beta and halting hypoxia-driven transcription.

steps.tx: Postoperative immunotherapy prevents recurrence following nephrectomy in high-risk localized disease. **Adjuvant pembrolizumab** for 1 year significantly improves disease-free and overall survival in resected intermediate-high and high-risk renal cell carcinoma in KEYNOTE-564. Overall survival was significantly prolonged with an HR of 0.62, representing the first adjuvant systemic therapy to demonstrate an overall survival advantage in RCC.

steps.tx: Non-clear cell histologies exhibit distinctive genetic alterations and require individualised management. **Non-clear cell RCC** variants include papillary RCC associated with MET alterations, chromophobe RCC exhibiting wholesale chromosomal losses, and aggressive collecting duct carcinoma. Papillary type 1 associates with germline or somatic MET mutations sensitive to cabozantinib, while collecting duct tumours require platinum-gemcitabine chemotherapy.
